blindSummary:
This country is among the most dangerous countries in the world for any LGBT person. A 1964 penal code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 3 years), but the operative reality is worse: an insurgent organisation controls significant territory and applies its interpretation of religious law, under which homosexuality and gender transgression are capital offences — executions are documented. Even in government-held areas, mob violence and informal lineage-based justice dynamics make any gender nonconformity a lethal risk. There is no legal gender recognition, no community, and no recourse of any kind.

For a visitor: there is no safe way to be visibly trans anywhere in the country.
blindOutOfScope: Fragmented authority means enforcement varies by area; insurgent-held areas apply capital punishment.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust's country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex sexual activity (up to life imprisonment under the 1964 penal code; death penalty under religious law in some regions).

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 3 years); the insurgent group enforces strict religious law with death as a possible punishment; pervasive violence and absence of state protection.
The same foreign government's 2022 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - continued criminalisation, insurgent executions, and no protections for LGBT persons.

The same foreign government's archived 2010 human-rights report on this country: documents the conflict, insurgent abuses, and an LGBT section noting criminalisation and the death penalty under religious law in areas under insurgent control.

Advocacy news site (Feb 2016): a legal advocate's report on the treatment of gay persons in this country sustains asylum claims - beyond the 3-year anti-homosexuality law, the insurgent group's religious-law enforcement may punish homosexuality by death; UN and foreign-government return guidance identifies gay persons as a 'risk profile'.

International news network (July 2013): gay, lesbian and HIV-positive refugees in a neighbouring country face death threats and persecution if returned; one journalist who fled the country says warlords have made it 'a death chamber for gays and lesbians'; another interviewee: 'It will be a massacre.'
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 3 years) and capital under the insurgent group's religious law — a catastrophic exposure for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
